title: Reference systems are pattern mines, not blueprints
statement: Reverse engineer an external system by problem/capability, extract transferable patterns and complexity, then run a gap analysis before architecture decisions.
applicability: Any product team studying external systems as references.

title: One entity, one identity, multiple views
statement: CRM, prospecting, map, agenda, reports and AI should operate on canonical entities rather than maintain parallel copies.
applicability: Systems with multiple modules/views over the same business entities.

title: AI over structured truth
statement: AI should consume selective structured context and propose actions; important writes pass through controlled domain operations and review rather than treating AI as the database.
applicability: AI-enabled operational systems with persistent business data.

title: Strangler migration with reversible vertical slices
statement: Replace legacy behavior incrementally with adapters, reconciliation, feature flags and rollback windows instead of a big-bang rewrite.
applicability: Brownfield migrations where continuity and rollback matter.

title: Professional gates may block release
statement: Environment or test limitations should block/label a release rather than be hidden or reported as success.
applicability: Release processes where environment/test uncertainty can hide risk.

title: Foundation plus visible user value
statement: Whenever safe, infrastructure packages should unlock a perceptible workflow improvement; UX polish should evolve with domain migration rather than as an isolated redesign.
applicability: Product migrations where infrastructure work must preserve user momentum.

title: Proportional ceremony by risk
statement: Use MICRO, STANDARD and STRUCTURAL paths so low-risk work stays fast while structural work receives evidence/architecture/safety discipline.
applicability: Any engineering/product workflow where one process risks becoming bureaucratic.

title: Machine store + generated human index
statement: Keep JSONL canonical for versioning/parsing while generating a readable index and metrics for human retrieval/adoption.
applicability: File-based knowledge stores that need both machine reliability and human browsing.
